market._comment: St. John's, Newfoundland — NOT South Florida. Earlier versions of this system inherited 'South Florida' from a placeholder in the original design brief and repeated it in every agent prompt; it was wrong. The Meta ad account bills in CAD, which is consistent with this.

outcomeStages._comment: This team does NOT use GHL's won/lost status — every opportunity sits at status 'open' and the outcome is signalled by dragging the card to a terminal column. Reading status alone returned null for all 149 leads, zeroing revenue and making the ROAS rule unfireable. These stage names are how won/lost is actually determined. 'Buyer Confirmed' and 'Listing Active' are NOT included as won — both carry deal values but are arguably mid-pipeline, so Jacob should confirm before counting them as revenue.

ghl._credentialsNote: Live GHL credentials are stored in the database (ghl_credentials), entered via the dashboard Settings page — not in this file.

meta._comment: Real estate IS a Meta restricted category (HOUSING), unlike Matama. This means no age/gender targeting, no sub-15mi radius, no lookalikes — the compliance gate in shared/meta/compliance.ts enforces this and cannot be overridden. Credentials live in the database, not here.

forge._comment: All values CAD. Grounded in real data pulled 2026-08-24 over a 30-day window: $1,131.37 total spend, $37.71/day actual, 3,203 clicks, $0.35 blended CPC. Client's own Meta daily budget is $50 ($30 buyers / $20 sellers).
forge.cplThresholdNote: UNVALIDATED. Zero leads carry ad attribution yet, so real CPL is unknown — at a 3% click-to-lead rate it would be ~$12, at 1% ~$35. Revisit once attribution produces the first 20-30 leads.
forge.roasNote: Rule DISABLED until revenue data is trustworthy. Only 4 of 149 leads carry a non-zero deal value. A rule that can never fire is worse than no rule — it looks like coverage that doesn't exist. Re-enable once outcomeStages above are confirmed and deal values are being recorded consistently.
forge.dailyBudgetCapNote: Was 500 — ten times the client's actual $50/day budget, so it was no guardrail at all. 75 allows 50% headroom to scale while still catching a runaway.
forge.fatigueThresholdNote: Was 0.7, which is mathematically impossible to stay under: frequency is impressions/reach, so any running ad is >= 1. All 63 ad sets exceeded it, meaning it would have flagged everything as fatigued forever. Their actual range is 1.48 avg / 1.88 max, so 3.0 sits above normal operation but still catches genuine fatigue.
